nodes.procedure: The copper mesh (300 mesh, 8×8 cm) was carefully cleaned in 1 wt% hydrochloric acid solution to remove impurities and oxides (termed the Cu filter).
nodes.source_text: The copper mesh (300 mesh, 8×8 cm) was carefully cleaned in 1 wt% hydrochloric acid solution to remove impurities and oxides (termed the Cu filter).

nodes.name: CuO nanowalls hydrothermal growth
nodes.procedure: Then, the Cu filter was soaked in a mixed aqueous solution of KOH (74.6 gL⁻¹) and (NH₄)₂S₂O₈ (15.2 gL⁻¹) and was subsequently heated at 100°C in an autoclave for 6 h. The obtained sample was termed the CuO electrochemical filter.

nodes.name: Co doping solvothermal and calcination
nodes.procedure: The CuO electrochemical filter was immersed into a mixed solution of 200 mL dimethylformamide and 300 mg cobalt acetylacetonate and then subject to a solvothermal process at 170°C for 4 h. The residual dimethylformamide and cobalt acetylacetonate on the sample surface are removed by deionized water and ethanol. The as-prepared sample was then calcined in an Ar atmosphere at 800°C for 2 h (with a ramp rate of 5°C min⁻¹). The final product was termed the Co-CuOx (an abbreviation of CoOx/CuOx) electrochemical filter.

nodes.source_text: The Co-CuOx filter was competent to reduce the aqueous nitrate concentration to a potable level (< 10 N-mg L⁻¹) at the flux of 60-120 L m⁻² h⁻¹ (Figure 5a). In addition, the removal of nitrate and TN decreased with an increase in the flux, that is, 95.2% of nitrate and 91.4% of TN were removed at a flux of 60 L m⁻² h⁻¹

The stability of the as-prepared Co-CuOx filter was evaluated in continuous operation at 60 L m⁻² h⁻¹ for 24 h (Figure 5d). Notably, the nitrate removal, the TN removal, and N2 FE of the Co-CuOx filter were maintained at 94.8±0.7, 90.5±0.8, and 57.2±3.8%, respectively.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy tests were carried out in a frequency range of 0.1 Hz to 100 kHz to investigate the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of the as-prepared filters... The plot of Co-CuOx exhibits an apparently smaller semicircle than those of other samples in the high-frequency range. These results indicated that the as-prepared Co-CuOx has the smallest charge transfer resistance (93.2 Ω)

In contrast to the electrocatalytic performance of Co-CuOx, selective conversion to N2 was unlikely for CuOx and Co3O4-CuO (Figure S18). NO2- and NH4+ were the primary reduction products in the reaction system of Co3O4-CuO over the onset potentials (-0.8 to -1.2 V vs Ag/AgCl) and ammonia achieved the maximum yield (10.5 N-mg L⁻¹ h⁻¹) at a potential of -1.2 V.

In contrast to the electrocatalytic performance of Co-CuOx, selective conversion to N2 was unlikely for CuOx and Co3O4-CuO (Figure S18). NO2- and NH4+ were the primary reduction products in the reaction system of Co3O4-CuO over the onset potentials (-0.8 to -1.2 V vs Ag/AgCl) and ammonia achieved the maximum yield (10.5 N-mg L⁻¹ h⁻¹) at a potential of -1.2 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniform nanowalls vertically grown on Cu filter surface for CuO and dense nanoclusters coated on vertical nanowalls for Co-CuOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images (Figures 1b,c and S7) show that uniform nanowalls were vertically grown on the entire surface of the Cu filter.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show nanoclusters of approximately 10 nm distributed on nanowall surfaces with homogeneous Cu, Co, and O elemental mapping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM images (Figures 1f-I and S8) further illustrate that the nanoclusters were distributed on the surface of nanowalls with a size of approximately 10 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Cu+ at 932.9/952.9 eV, Cu2+ at 934.1/954.2 eV, Co3+ at 779.9/794.7 eV, Co2+ at 781.5/796.2 eV, and oxygen vacancies at 531.2 eV in O 1s spectrum.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu 2p spectrum consists of two satellite peaks and two pairs of characteristic peaks. In detail, the peaks at 932.9 and 952.9 eV correspond to Cu+ 2p3/2 and Cu+ 2p1/2...

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS at Cu K-edge shows Cu-O at 1.61 Å, Cu-Cu at 2.17 Å with coordination number of Cu-O at 0.98 indicating abundant oxygen vacancies; Co K-edge shows Co-O at 1.55 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2e, the peaks at 1.61 and 2.17 Å of Co-CuOx are ascribed to Cu-O and Cu-Cu coordination, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show straight and sharp peaks indicating high crystallization in Co-CuOx electrochemical filter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns show straight and sharp peaks, indicating the high crystallization in the Co-CuOx electrochemical filter (Figure S12).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of Co-CuOx is 2.37 m²/g compared to 1.54 m²/g for CuO filter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These 3D nanostructures of Co-CuOx are favorable for the exposure of active sites, thereby leading to an enlarged specific surface area (2.37 m²g⁻¹) as compared to 1.54 m²g⁻¹ of the CuO filter (Figure S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV used to determine electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl for ECSA calculation: Co-CuOx 1.05 m²/g, CuOx 0.65 m²/g, Co3O4-CuO 0.90 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA of the as-prepared electrochemical filters were evaluated by the electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) under the potential window of no redox reactions (details in Section S2 and Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct of 93.2 Ω for Co-CuOx, 110.7 Ω for CuOx, 146.3 Ω for Co3O4-CuO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The plot of Co-CuOx exhibits an apparently smaller semicircle than those of other samples in the high-frequency range... Co-CuOx has the smallest charge transfer resistance (93.2 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS used to quantify leaching concentrations of Cu and Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The leaching concentrations of Cu and Co were quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (PerkinElmer NexION 300X).

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR with DMPO spin trapping shows weaker DMPO-H signal intensity for Co-CuOx compared to CuOx and Co3O4-CuO, indicating less H* contribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S24 shows that the peak intensity of DMPO-H for Co-CuOx is significantly weaker than those for CuOx and Co3O4-CuO.
